prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create ONE independent high-fidelity website concept "Une journée à Douala" for Continental Group. A bold contemporary documentary publication translated into a business homepage with scrollytelling. Target dimensions 1440 x 2160, a single long scrollable marketing page. The image is the website itself, full bleed edge to edge, no device, no browser, no surrounding board and no explanatory annotations.
Reference 1 is an OLD Continental homepage, ONLY a source of business context and an ANTI-reference for visual structure. Do not repeat its split hero, portrait collage, cream backgrounds, serif headline, repeated cards or rounded masks. Reference 2 supplies the existing official green and gold Continental Group logo, preserve brand spelling and recognizable identity.
Make the layout radically different from a standard corporate template: a compact publication-like navigation bar, then a full-width photographic opening with type BELOW the photograph rather than placed in a side panel. Strong editorial picture editing, no little eyebrow above every heading. No card grid anywhere.
Regions in order:
- Header 80px: authentic logo left, normal-case links "Le Groupe", "Nos métiers", "Contact". Small location "Douala, Cameroun". White background.
- Opening photograph 620px high, spanning the entire page width: a candid proposed documentary street scene in contemporary Douala, a ground-level wide view outside an ordinary well-maintained local shop, Black Cameroonian people moving a packaged household appliance and everyday urban activity, tropical roadside vegetation, humid morning sunlight, concrete surfaces, authentic physical texture, no safari imagery, no skyscraper fantasy, no invented store logos. This is an art direction image, not a claim about an actual Continental property. Subject should be off-center, with cinematic depth, no posed models staring at viewer. Rich naturally colored reportage quality with careful composition.
- Beneath photograph a very large single confident typographic line "Douala, au quotidien." in an expressive but highly readable medium-width grotesk, dark true green ink on clean white. Place a SHORT 2-line supporting paragraph to one side UNDER this heading, not beside the opening photograph: "Commerce, énergie, logiciels et soin textile. Quatre métiers pour les besoins des entreprises et des familles." On the same clear reading surface provide the four direct links "Market", "Energy", "Software", "Pressing" and one main plain rectangular action "Découvrir le groupe". Sparse, purposeful navigation, no pills, no cards, no decorative badges.
- Next story passage roughly 700px: make a visually striking asymmetrical editorial composition within the same white page. At left, a narrow but readable story text column "La journée commence." with the copy "S'équiper pour la maison et le travail." and the link "Continental Market". A very wide shop-detail photograph runs across the lower-right two-thirds: the real texture of shelving, packaged electronics, hands preparing a purchase, no generic showroom. A small contrasting documentary crop at the extreme page edge may show a power installation; purposeful picture sequence, not a collage of portraits. Show the next chapter beginning "L'activité continue." so the scroll narrative is evident. Treat the image as the region that will hold while the story text changes.
- Final region: a calm typographic contact line "Retrouvons-nous à Logpom." and "Nous contacter", plus modest remaining business links. Do not fabricate numbers or case studies.
Visual system: mostly true white, rich forest-green typography, small official yellow logo accent only, photographic terracotta and concrete colors come from the actual scene. No beige parchment theme, no fake newspaper grain, no generic serif, no thin-rule fetish, no bright-yellow CTA pattern. Typography resembles carefully spaced Archivo or an expressive documentary grotesk, at most two fonts, body at least equivalent to 16px at 1440px. Large breathing spaces interrupted by decisive wide photographs. One striking layout move at a time. It must look like a studio art-directed a site about this actual city and these actual activities. No UI implementation jargon, animation labels, dates, invented guarantees, stats, testimonials or awards. Correct French throughout. One concept only.
status: concept - photography generated for art direction, not documentary evidence
